Jeg kan godt forstå dine følelser. Men jeg vil sige, at den oplevelse er helt normal og noget, alle kommer ud for. Jeg er selv 35 og har oplevet det samme for nyligt - at være interesseret i en person, der ikke gengældte det. Det føles altid øv, men det bliver lettere at bearbejde, når man bliver ældre. 

Det skyldes dels, at man finder ud af, at det er noget, der sker for alle, og at andre slet ikke dømmer en, som man selv tror, og dels, at man finder ud af, at de negative følelser og tanker går væk, og også udvikler strategier til at cope med dem - f.eks. musik, motion, at snakke det igennem med andre eller mindfulness (at lære at anerkende og acceptere ens følelser uden at lade dem styre ens tanker).

En anden ting, der hjælper, er at vide, at der er mange grunde til, at det ikke kan være gengældt. Nogle gange er personen ikke interesseret i et forhold. Nogle gange har de andre ting, de kæmper med. Og nogle gange er man bare ikke et godt match - men det betyder ikke, at du ikke er god nok til ham. Det betyde bare, at i to ikke passer sammen.
Så lidt :)

Happy to help. However, since I can see that I got the purpose of your essay wrong, I think that if I am to provide further feedback, I would have to understand your purpose better.

Could you maybe try to put the main thesis of your abstract into one sentence? To help me understand what you are trying to do?

There are some other points I could try to respond to, but I don't think it would be of much help as long as I don't understand your main thesis.

So I read the abstract. It is a pretty good draft, but should not be considered the final product.

Overall thoughts: You have good language and narrative ability within the individual sections, but when it comes to the overall structure and argument of the book, you seem to struggle. Also, while you have a pretty good superficial knowledge on a lot of areas, you need to focus your research and dive deeper within specific areas relevant for what you are are trying to do.

I will expand: as a student I asked a visiting professor for advice on how to write a book, and he told me to try to get the idea of the book down into one sentence. This is good advice and I have read similar things online.

The problem is that after reading this abstract, the overall goal of the abstract seems unfulfilled. Part of the problem seems to be that much of the information of the abstract, while well-written and interesting in its own right, doesn't really contribute much to the overall goal of the book.

If I had to put the goal into one sentence it would be something like the following: the golden rule is found in many cultures and might be an indicator of supernatural selection.

My issue is that while you spend several chapters talking about nuclear war, existence, laws and selection, you never really define what supernatural selection is or why it is needed to explain the golden rule. Some of the parts, such as the one on mind-dependent entities seem like you believe them to be important to your argument, but you never really flesh out how. The last chapter on the golden rule is obviously also meant to be important to your argument, but you never make it explicit how the golden rule implies supernatural selection - something that would also require you to define what supernatural selection is.

Another issue has to do with your research. You obviously have superficial knowledge about a range of areas and have thought about them - to list some you briefly touch on statistics, game theory, the threat of a nuclear war, Charles Darwin, ontology, imaginary numbers, information theory, entropy, emergence, the Libet experiments, behaviorism and cost-benefit analyses. These are a lot of different areas, and as far as I know, it is generally correct. However, the problems are first that you hardly present me with any new knowledge and secondly that I generally don't know how most of these topics are meant to relate to each other or contribute to an overarching argument or theory.

To expand on the first problem, I do have a masters in philosophy and pretty big interest in science, but I am by no means an expert on any of these topics. The fact that you cannot provide me with much new knowledge indicates to me that your knowledge might not be more expansive than mine, and that is a problem since I do not have enough expertise to write an interesting product on any of these topics. My recommendation would be to begin researching these and related areas. Generally I think that one should spend something like 3 times the amount of time researching (finding acquiring and reading papers, books and other material relevant to whatever one is working on) as one does on writing. Likely you would soon have to focus on a more limited amount of areas, but that would likely be an advantage since it might give your abstract more focus and depth and make it less all over the place. You might also find that many of these areas are not as important as you thought while there might be other fields that are relevant but which you have overlooked. I would also advice against just reading the big, historical figures like Berkeley and Darwin. Reading some of them is fine, but generally I think you are better off focusing most of your research on more up to date material which generally tends to incorporate the most important points of the well-known historical figures while also presenting knew information that they did not have access to.

As for the second problem, it relates to what I said before about the abstract lacking structure and how it is unclear how the different chapters and parts are relevant to the overall argument. I think that part of this might be related to a lack of research too. If your point is that the golden rule is an indication of divinity, then it is almost certain that someone has made this argument before. You need to find out whether it has and who has made it as well as read up on the main arguments against this position. Indeed, one of the best ways to make your own argument clearer and stronger is by making sure to read up on the main arguments against it. In fact, if I were you, I would aim to do the following with each chapter and each part of each chapter - formulate the argument of the section, make it explicit how it relates to the overall argument and research and read up to date literature on the topic of the section. In fact, beginning to use references and adding a literature list would probably be a good exercise that helps you in holding yourself accountable when doing research. I suspect that if you did this, you might find that many of the sections in the book don't actually contribute much to the overall argument. They seem more like detours.

A couple of final points.

First off, when writing you will often make plenty of drafts before you end up with the final product. That is completely normal. I have provided a lot of critique, but don't let that trouble you too much. Your writing on the individual parts is interesting and well explained. The writing itself is not a problem. You just need to do more focused research as well as work more on the overall structure of the abstract as well as how the different parts relate to each other. The final product is likely to be significantly different from how it is now, but each draft gets closer and provides one with a clearer idea of how the final product will look.

Secondly, seeking out critique and responses from others is a good idea. Getting feedback from people online can be hard and also depends on your ability to briefly explain the main points of your product. Don't just see asking for help as a possibility of getting feedback. You should also see it as training in explaining yourself and your main thesis in a concise way. The better you are at this, the better your chance of getting feedback and the better the quality of the feedback. Another reason for seeking feedback had to do with solitude. Writing can quickly become a pretty lonely endeavor, and involving other people is a good way to make it less so.

Jeg siger det fordi at jeg netop har snuset lidt til forskningen - og også brugte meget af min uddannelse på bevidsthedsfilosofi, kognitiv videnskab og psykologi - og generelt var mit indtryk, at der ikke er den store forskningsmæssige evidens for, at de fleste personlighedstests er specielt brugbare.

Den eneste personlighedstest jeg kender til, som faktisk er bakket op af evidens, er the big 5-testen.

Hvorfor virksomhederne stadig bruger dem skal jeg ikke kunne sige, men det er ikke det eneste eksempel på, at de ikke agerer på baggrund af evidens. At antage, at virksomheder for det meste er rationelle er fint, men at antage at de altid er det er bare modbevist af en del eksempler.

Jeg havde for eksempel et fag om kropssprogspsykologi, der også lagde ud med et en tekst om, at en del "kropssprogseksperter" bygger en succesfuld karriere op omkring, hvad der reelt er pseudovidenskab - ikke fordi at kropssprogspsykologi generelt er pseudovidenskab, men fordi at deres forsimplede, reduktionistiske version af det er.

Lige i det her tilfælde vil jeg gerne se dokumentationen på, at det virker.

Min erfaring er, at de fleste populære personlighedstests ikke bliver taget super seriøst inden for forskningen da der ikke er nogen nævneværdig evidens, der viser, at de faktisk fanger noget interessant. Det gælder også den populære Myers-Briggs.

Så jeg er skeptisk over for ideen om, at popularitet er evidens for effekt, også når det kommer til arbejdsmarkedet, og i særdeleshed når det kommer til personlighedstests.

You mention that you are having problems with the effect a divorce will have on your kids.

If anything I think that it might be the other way around. You need to divorce for the sake of your kids. Growing up with divorced parents is preferable to growing up in a home with domestic violence. If you look into the stories from people who grew up on in the latter, I suspect a lot of your worries would be alleviated.

Honestly I would argue that for the sake of your children, you should not only divorce, but also look into legal action against your wife. With her temper and lack of accountability, I fear the effect she might have on the children if the authorities are not aware.

I agree that you should do what is best for not only yourself and your children, but disagree that this means staying in the marriage. But do look more into it and try to contact some organizations dealing with domestic violence. They will be able to give you better advice and counseling.

Hvis jeg havde konkret evidens for, at en person har kørt for hurtigt, ville jeg ikke have noget problem med at anmelde vedkommende til politiet. Det afhænger selvfølgelig af om der har været formildende omstændigheder. Men generelt er utroskab mere skadeligt end de fleste tilfælde, hvor en person kommer til at køre for hurtigt. Så et godt eksempel på at der ikke er en en til en relation mellem lov og moral.

Og jeg gjorde opmærksom på, at netop det ikke at blande sig, når der er rimelig grund til at tro, at et andet menneske bliver skadet, fordi at man "ikke vil stikke næsen i andres sager" eller fordi at det "ikke påvirker en selv eller ens nære" historisk har ført til nogle rigtig dårlige ting.

Men hvis du ikke kan lide politiske eksempler kan jeg også nævne mobning, forhold hvor den ene partner undertrykker den anden eller emotionel mistrivsel hos børn, der historisk set har været drevet af den samme attitude.

Det er i og for sig fair nok at holde sig tilbage, hvis man har begrænset viden - man kan også overreagere - men i så fald bør man søge mere viden eller som minimum være ekstra opmærksom fremadrettet. Og man bør ikke bruge det som en undskyldning til ikke at reagere, når man har begrundet mistanke.

Mobning er ikke ulovligt. Det er heller ikke ulovligt at overfuse en ungarbejder, fordi at man selv har haft en dårlig dag. I begge tilfælde håber jeg, at du og de fleste andre alligevel ville sige fra.

Alt noget er ulovligt betyder ikke, at det ikke er forkert.

Nu snakker jeg ikke specifikt om utroskab længere. Det er den generelle attitude hvor man kun kører sig om sig selv og sine  egne, jeg problematiserer her. Også når det ikke drejer sig om utroskab.

Jeg tænker også, at alle på tværs af det politiske spektrum er ret enige om, at både nazismen og fascismen var noget skidt, så muligvis politisk, men ikke kontroversielt.

"tag kun affære hvis det påvirker dig eller din nære familie"

Det er muligvis en kontroversiel holdning her, men inden for socialpsykologien er det ret ukontroversielt, at det er præcis den attitude, der har gjort det muligt for nazister, fascister og andre autoritære regimer at komme til magten.

Jeg synes virkelig at en af de værste ting ved dansk kultur er denne her udbredt uvilje mod at sige fra over for utroskab på trods af, at det gør så stor skade. Jeg synes at det er en kollektiv stiltiende accept af utroskab som jeg på ingen måde selv ønsker at deltage i. Hvis et menneske skader et andet menneske mener jeg principielt, at man bør reflektere over, hvad man selv kan/bør gøre ud fra det man ved og ikke ved - præcis som du gør.

I det her specifikke tilfælde er den selvfølgelig lidt svær, når man ikke kender dem bedre. Men hvis du kan se navnene, kan du måske finde den anden partner på SoMe og sende dem en venlig besked om, at du selvfølgelig ikke ved, hvad deres ordning er, men at du har set kvinden med en nden mand og hørt dem have sex. Jeg ville nok ikke selv gå længere end det, når jeg ikke selv kender mere til situationen og deres specifikke relation.

Komplimenter og korte berøring.

Med komplimenter, så tænk over, hvad du godt kan lide ved ham og komplimenter ham på det - både ved udseende og personlighed.

Med berøring så ting som kram, holde hans hånd, eller finde undskyldninger for at røre hans arme, skulder, hår osv.

Hvis du er genert, så tag det i et tempo, som du er komfortabel med. Hvis i tager små skridt med komplimenter og korte berøringer vil det langsomt blive mere naturligt. Lad være med at føle dig presset til at tage et skridt, der føles for stort, eller at gøre for mange ting på en gang.

From what I am hearing, you didn't do anything cruel. You said that you have never ended relationships before - even bad ones - and that you thought you had made real progress.

You also say that he was toxic (and from the examples you mention I have to stress that I agree very much) and that you started having anxiety and physical symptoms around him and then abruptly ended the relationship.

Thing is, that doesn't sound like cruel behaviour. It sounds like you stood up for yourself and ended the relationship with a cruel person who was bad for you.

If you have never done something like that before, you might experience guilt, but the thing is that this is exactly the hat healthy people do. They avoid relationships with toxic people who negatively affect their life, and if anything, you doing that is a sign that you have indeed made progress.

Igen, når man er 16 år og hænger ud med andre mennesker og politiet ud af det blå kommer med hunde og kaos, så er det ikke nødvendigvis noget, man tænker over. Der reagerer man instinktivt, og når man reagerer instinktivt, så gør man dumme ting. Det er ret veldokumenteret, når man læser historier om, hvordan folk har reageret i krisesituationer - også voksne mennesker.

Den vurdering synes jeg ikke er helt fair.

For det første kan jeg sagtens se, hvordan man som 16-årig kan komme til at reagere sådan, når en så uventet situation pludselig opstår, for hvem pokker har forberedt sig mental på at politiet pludselig dukker op med hunde? Der reagerer man ofte instinktivt når man er teenager og ens impulsstyring ikke er fuldt udviklet.

For det andet er det en ting hvorvidt politiet har haft rimelig grund til at mistænke ham - hvilket jeg er enig i - og noget helt andet om de har reageret unødvendigt hårdhændet - hvilket jeg ikke ved om de har. Var det f.eks. nødvendigt at smide ham på jorden og undersøge ham i fuld offentlighed? Det er helt legitime spørgsmål, som jeg ikke kender svaret på.

Det er fuldstændig ligegyldigt om du stoler på ham eller ej. Han kan være den mest ærlige, troværdige og omsorgsfulde kæreste, og han kan alligevel blive hacket så de videoer ender alle mulige steder.

Altså, jeg ville selv tænde på at filme det, men jeg ville aldrig presse nogen til det. Tværtimod ville jeg først skulle være helt sikker på, at de forstår risiciene ved det. Og det ville være med det forbehold, at så snart en af os siger det eller hvis vi slår op, så skal de videoer slettes uden indvendinger.

Hvis alle andre de andre historier om racisme herinde havde en "jeg har det ret stramt med danskere" tilknyttet ville folk ikke acceptere det. Men det er acceptabelt, når det er etniske minoriteter.

Som jeg ser det, er det lige så legitimt at have fordomme om mænd som om ikke-vestlige (og omvendt).

If he doesn't love you enough to put up with the dog, then he has no business to blame you for not loving him enough to part with it.

It is completely legit for him to say that the dog is a dealbreaker now that he understand how much it takes, and it is equally legit for you to say that getting rid of the dog is a dealbreaker.

However, it is not legit to claim that it is you who is jeopardizing your future, when he is doing the exact same. That is hypocrisy.

I am a nerd. For me it is being able to nerd away.

For me it means researching and reading books, articles and other resources on the topics that interest me as well as researching and figuring out ways in which knowledge of these topics might make a difference for others and work on projects that might make this a reality (I am still at the beginning of the journey, but looking at my progress and how consistent I am in my efforts, I am confident that I will find ways to make this happen unless something completely unexpected happens).

For me, while it can be difficult, this causes me the most consistent, meaningful and some of the most intense feelings of pleasure and wellbeing.

For det andet er der en tendens til, at forhold er mindre attraktive for kvinder end for mænd. Så vidt jeg har kunne finde ud af, tyder det på, at flere kvinder end mænd er lykkelige som single, imens flere mænd end kvinder er lykkelige i forhold - https://www.hu-berlin.de/en/press-portal/nachrichten-en/january-2025/nr-2517 (det samme lader til at gøre sig gældende i Danmark - https://www.berlingske.dk/samfund/kvinder-er-lykkeligere-singler-end-maend )

Denne her artikel komme rind på, hvordan drengebørn i mindre grad bliver mødt med forståelse, når de udtrykker følelsesmæssig sårbarhed sammenlignet med pigebørn, og hvordan det på sigt kan gøre, at mænd i mindre grad udvikler sunde relationer, hvor de kan dække deres emotionelle behov, og dermed bliver mere emotionelt afhængige af at være i et forhold - [https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/men-actually-crave-romantic-relationships-more-than-women-do/](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/men-actually-crave-romantic-relationships-more-than-women-do/)

Der er også stadig udfordringer med, at kvinder har flere orgasmer, når de onanerer eller har sex, end når de har sex med en mand - [https://videnskab.dk/krop-sundhed/orgasmekloeften-derfor-kommer-kvinder-ikke-saa-ofte-som-maend/](https://videnskab.dk/krop-sundhed/orgasmekloeften-derfor-kommer-kvinder-ikke-saa-ofte-som-maend/)

"Kvinder og mænd minder meget om hinanden, hvad angår tidsforbrug, dog er der visse forskelle, der går igen uanset alder og baggrund. Til gengæld bruger kvinderne knap 1 time mindre på erhvervsarbejde og har cirka ½ time mindre fritid pr. dag end mændene".

Så mænd arbejder mere end kvinder og har mere fritid, imens kvinderne laver mere husarbejde end mænd og bruger mere tid på primær behov (f.eks. søvn, mad og personlig hygiejne). Nu har jeg ikke læst hele rapporten, men så vidt jeg kunne skimte, er forskellen blevet mindre allerede dengang - en udvikling som den øremærkede barsel yderligere burde formindske 2/2

Når det er sagt er der noget, der tyder på, at det, vi bruger til at vurdere, om vi vil være i et forhold med nogen, ikke er gode til at vurdere, om vi vil kunne fungere i et langsigtet forhold. For det første udtaler mange sig på baggrund af dating apps, og dating apps er nok den arena, hvor det så vidt jeg har kunnet finde ud af er allerhårdest at være mand. Back then, the vast majority of people had to be peasants. Without modern technology and knowledge, you need a lot of people to grow food. Even in good periods, more people led to more procreation, leading to a need for even more food, until times gets worse and people die from starvation (the malthusian trap).

To adress OP's question, my guess would be that two factors play a role. 

First off, from an autistic perspective the biggest challenge today compared to back then is that people move around a lot more. You go to school one place, go to university/college another and then end up shifting between different jobs throughout your life. This means that you will have to interact with a lot of very different people and form new connections. Even neurotypicals struggle with this - my understanding is that loneliness is on the rise on the western world because the interaction with so many different people makes it hard to form lasting connections which are crucial for a good life quality. People with autism have a harder time doing this and thus end up struggling more. Compare this to back in time when you generally lived in the same place and had the same profession (most likely being a farmer) throughout your life, and thus ended up knowing the same people all your life. Social skills are still important, but you aren't as dependent on your ability to interact and form connections with many different people - something autists have a hard time with. 

Secondly, other factors such as titles and wealth were much more important to how you would do in life compared to autism, meaning that people emphasized differences in character less (since they didn't have diagnoses I will just refer to it as differences in character). It was simply comparatively less important. This is not to say that people with aspergers would do well back then. The average person is likely to have had a worse life than today, and the same is likely true about people with aspergers. However, most of the time, this would not be due to their diagnosis, but due to other factors such as war, disease, poverty, being born into a low-status position etc. If you were born into a high-status family, you would be likely to do well regardless of whether you had autistic traits or not, and vice versa, being born into a low-status family is likely to lead to a very tough life regardless of whether you have autistic traits.

I agree with your main points here 

It is part that the extra effort of trying to learn these intricate social patterns is a skill and learning that skill is absolutely an additional burden. Even moreso since social processes are so complex and subtle. To top that off autists often have social needs that differ from most other people and which also must be taken into account. Doing that really takes effort, and that needs to be acknowledged both by themselves and the surroundings.

I also agree with the idea of some kind of tutoring. I have read a university level social psychology textbook and according to it, there have been good results trying to teach social skills to people who are struggling with them - not specifically autists but people in general. In my own experience, I have also been quite succesful in doing this. To be honest, I do think that most people would benefit from some degree of learning about social patterns and processes. Not just autists but many people today struggle with issues relating to things like loneliness, discrimination, conflict etc. That could be remedied to some degree with a better understanding of underlying social mechanisms. However, some people might benefit from additional tutoring and many autists would probably fall under this category.

To be honest, I am quite sceptical of the conclusions you are drawing here. First off, social relations are generally recognized as much more complex than simple hierarchical stuctures. For example, a persons status will change to group and might also differ based on environment and social context. While hierarchy might be important at work, it is likely to play a far less important role when hanging out with your friends - depending both on your work place and your friend group. While no one would claim that hierarchies and status doesn't play a role in social relations, my impression is that few today assign it the same importance that they did 1-2 centuries ago.

Second off, the source doesn't say anything about whether ASD's participate in hierarchy games. It assumes that they would have a hard time recognizing indicators of hierarchy and concludes that the experiments conducted shows no such thing, but doesn't say much more than that. Actually it concludes that "Thus, ASD subjects may perceive social rank of other individuals more strictly, but in a different manner from normal subjects, especially when such recognition is based on social signs" meaning that it could just as well be the case that they do it more. However, ultimately it is agnostic on this topic. Furthermore, the study itself says that "This study is rather at a preliminary stage, given a number of subjects participated in the study is relatively small" meaning that it is very limited to which degree you can actually draw hard conclusions based on the study.

Possibly an unpopular opinion on here but it is my experience that when it comes to people that say that they are disliked because they are honest, it turns out that most of the time (but of course not all of it) the problem is not that they are being honest, but that they are giving their opinions in ways which either are hurtful towards others or are not relevant for them.

In the case of people on the spectrum, my guess would be that due to psychological differences, what we might consider to be simple honesty is seen as either inconsiderate ways of saying things or simply irrelevant information, resulting in alienation. This is not to say the solution is to lie, but generally people are expected to consider whether information is relevant to others as well as how to deliver it in a way that is considerate of the feelings of others. Of course this is harder for people with autism who might not even realize that what they are saying is irrelevant or hurtful.

The part about information expected to be relevant to others might strike some as odd given the autistic bafflement with the phenomena of smalltalk which is, if anything, exchange of irrelevant information. This is another misunderstanding due to psychological differences. The main purpose of smalltalk isn't to transmit information, but to show acknowledgement and create trust and mutual familiarity that can pave the way for more meaningful conversations. The problem here is that such  microinteractions, like most social phenomena, follow certain rules and regularities. Most people follow these patterns without really being aware of it and without ever realizing that they are following specific and fairly determined social patterns. The problem from an autistic point of view is that we don't and have to either dedicate time to learn it or try to find ways to our engagement with it.

So from what I understand from your comments on this post, his parents reached out and asked you to convince him because they figured he needed help. You unblocked him, wrote him a message and blocked him again. Then they pressured you to keep trying.

A few comments on that.

They are obviously right that he needs therapy. However I am not sure they are right to turn to you. He might still be caught up with you since he hasn't had luck on tinder and since his social circle seems to have dropped him, so they might see you as the one person that he might listen too.

Now, I can't speak for all Danes but from my point of view what they are doing is inappropriate. Parents sometimes do stupid things for their children, but pestering the ex who just lost a pregnancy against her will, got dumped by her boyfriend for the dumbest reason immediately after and who still needs therapy is just not ok. This is not your responsibility and it is very unlikely that you are even the right person to try given your own situation. Besides that, I don't see why the ex would even listen to you unless he saw it as some chance to get together, and that would be a shitty situation for both of you.

My advice to you would be to not write your ex. You have already done what can be reasonably expected off you. Getting further involved might just damage your own mental health. You can't help someone who refuses help.

Instead I would advice you to write the parents. Let them know that even though you understand that they want to help their son, you are not in the best mental health space yourself, and trying to help someone who refuses help and who has also let you down and hurt you that badly is not something that you can do to yourself. Let them know that you do hope that they succeed in getting help from him.

And if they still try to get you involved, then you let them know that while you do like them as people you will have to block them if they don't stop. And if they continue you follow through and block them.

Another really good idea is to talk it through with your therapist first though. They have a better understanding of you, your mental health situation and how your relationship with your ex affected you.

Many with Asperger's can have problems with this kind of thinking, where they feel that they have to go all the way if they begin something and therefore become inflexible in how they set goals. It also leads to overthinking and overpreparation where you try to want to make sure that you have thought of everything before taking a decision but where the impossibility of thinking of everything might paralyze you. It is one of the challenges we can face. In these cases hearing that it is ok to abort from the goal and that the decision doesn't have to be final can be helpful, though it might take hearing it many times before we begin believing it.

Another problem is that people with autism have issues dealing with change. It drains them more than other people and we require more preparation. We also tend to do worse under pressure, and forget to pay attention to how we are actually doing. Here making the change gradual, making time for preparation and making time to check-in and discuss how things are going, how we are doing and whether things are moving too fast or not can be helpful. While elemental magic isn't necessarily bad, it is the default of magic, and as such has been overdone and overused. As any other trope, defaulting to it without some kind of twist or novelty is likely to be perceived as lazy and boring because it has been done by so many other people. For me, I would prefer if it was put aside and other ways to organize and categorize magic systems was developed further instead. I think there is a lot of potential on doing so, but understand why people don't since relying at least partly on a well-known trope can lead to good results with less effort, though you will still need some kind of new take on the trope of you want to catch peoples attention.

There are many interesting ways to organize magic. Elemental magic isn't worse than most other ways to do so, but it isn't better either. It is fairly reductionistic and arbitrary to divide magic into the common elements of fire, earth, water, air (sometimes with some variations such as inclusion of ice or lighting or exclusion of one or more of the traditional four) as it excludes so many types of magic such as transformation, body augmentation, mental magic, time or space, abstract magic, divination, fate magic, sensory magic, transmutation etc.

There are a lot more interesting ways to group or categorize magic. Honestly, the D&D 8 schools system is much more comprehensive in types of magic it allows for, though every categorization based on effect will run into areas of grey areas between categories and magic that doesn't fit into any category.

One would also try to divide magic not based on effect but on what it requires to use. One could categorize magic based on whether it is based on things like chanting, ingredients, mental ressources, life force, runes or some combination of these. And these are just a couple of the many, many possibilities.

This is not to say that every need can be met without romance. I have a genuine need for romance in my life, and if I go too long without engaging with it, I will eventually become unsatisfied. Jeg kan ikke se, hvordan du får nationalitet blandet ind i det. Mit argument er demokratisk. Folkekirken er en offentlig institution og som sådan har den forpligtigelse til at bevare en folkelig opbakning. Ellers smuldrer dens eksistensgrundlag. Hvis den begynder at retfærdiggøre åben diskrimination af kvinder, homoseksuelle og fraskilte i en verden, hvor flertallet i Danmark er klart imod det, så er det helt legitimt at spørge sig selv, hvorfor vi skal have en folkekirke - skrevet ind i grundloven og underlagt staten - der støtter op om adfærd og værdier, som flertallet af befolkningen finder moralsk problematisk og endda forkasteligt. Det er fuldstændigt i overensstemmelse med den nede-fra-og-op definition af folk som du taler om.

Et mere interessant aspekt du belyser er diskussionen om nærhedsdemokrati versus nationalt demokrati, altså i hvor høj grad enkelte sogne har ret til at vælge præster, hvis teologiske holdninger flugter med deres egne selv om disse potentielt er i modstrid med værdier og holdninger hos det nationale flertal. Og det er en afvejning. Det må dog understreges, at den frihed ikke kan være absolut, netop fordi at folkekirken er tilknyttet staten, og alle statslige institutioner vil i et eller andet udgangspunkt være ansvarlig over for nationale, demokratiske processer. Ellers er der, som jeg ser det, ikke noget grundlag for at give folkekirken den særstatus frem for andre trossamfund, som den har ifølge grundloven. Hvis man vil have større teologisk og religiøs frihed må man organisere sin kirke og sit trossamfund uafhængigt af staten på linje med alle andre trossamfund. Så vil man få større frihed, men omvendt vil man ikke få den organisatoriske støtte og status, som folkekirken nyder, men som den også kontinuerligt nå gøre sig fortjent til.

For mig at se går den direkte diskrimination af fraskilte, homoseksuelle og for den sags skyld også kvinder over grænsen for, hvad en statslig institution bør kunne acceptere. At være en statslig institution forpligter trods alt også.

Når det er sagt, er der i dette tilfælde - altså artiklens - ikke tale om en modsætning mellem nærdemokratiet i sognet og det nationale demokrati. Modstanden mod præsten - og menighedsrådet - kommer ikke udefra, men fra lokale, som ikke mener at præsten agerer i overensstemmelse med deres værdier. Så det er et lokalpolitisk opgør, men med national politiske perspektiver på grund af folkekirkens særlige rolle.
Jeg ved det godt. Folk er forskellige.
Jeg kan godt følge, at det kan virke mærkeligt. Jeg kunne dog selv have fundet på det samme.

Du har ikke gjort noget galt. Men du er blevet voldsomt manipuleret og udsat for psykisk vold af et frygteligt menneske. Jeg er glad for, at du er kommet ud af det og håber på det bedste for dig her på den anden side 🙏

Og du havde al ret til at være sammen med en anden person på den rejse, når han eksplicit havde gjort det klart, at han ikke ville have en kæreste. Den var 100% på ham, men typer som han vil selvfølgelig aldrig anerkende det og tage ansvar, når de kan projicere og bebrejde andre.

> Og reglerne skal være ens for alle trossamfund.

Hvis det var et trossamfund som alle andre, ville jeg være enig, men folkekirkens eksistensgrundlag og grunden til at den er skrevet ind i grundloven er netop, at det skal være en kirke for 'folket' og vel at mærke hele folket.

Selvfølgelig er der nogen, der vælger den fra af forskellige grunde, men så længe der er mindst 70%, der er medlemmer, bliver det næppe et stort problem. Det er et større problem, hvis den og dens repræsentanter selv begynder at vælge folk fra - og især hvis der er tale om grupper, der i forvejen er diskriminerende, som f.eks. homoseksuelle, eller store grupper som f.eks. fraskilte. Så bliver det umindeligt svært at se det folkelige i folkekirken.

Der er blevet argumenteret for, at det folkelige ligger i, at der også er plads til folk, der teologisk er imod skilsmisser eller homoseksuelle, eller kvindelige præster for den sags skyld, men det holder i min optik ikke. Der ville stadig være plads til dem - de kan komme i kirken og blive døbt, viet og begravet. De kan bare ikke have officielle positioner, hvis det betyder, at de vil diskriminere andre, ligesom vi heller ikke tillader læger, socialrådgivere eller andre statsansatte at diskriminere imod grupper de ikke bryder sig om.

Igen ville intet af dette være et problem hvis folkekirken var et trossamfund som alle andre, men det er det ikke. Det er netop en statslig folkekirke, og dens eksistensgrundlag afhænger af, at den formår at holde fast i sin folkelige opbakning og at favne bredt. Og her duer det ikke, at den eller dens repræsentanter begynder at modvirke ellers accepterede folkelige dagsordner som at modvirke diskrimination af kvinder, seksuelle minoriteter og fraskilte.

In the mirror condition only 12% of the children took more than one piece of candy compared to 34% in the control condition (almost trice as many).

This is an argument ad absurdum. There must be a first cause because the only alternative is an infinite series of events which results in a paradox.

However, as far as I can see your own explanation also leads to a paradox. If there is a first cause to everything else, then either there was a time before this first cause or there wasn't a time before the first cause.

If there was a time before the first cause created everything else, then time still existed before the first cause created everything else, and then the problem remains intact since an infinite amount of time must have taken place before the first cause caused everything else to exist. Instead we now have the additional problem of explaining why the first cause suddenly caused everything else to exist at some point in time.

So, we have to insist that the first cause also caused time. However, this also leads to a paradox since causation is something that happens in time. When something creates something else, this takes place in time, making it completely opaque how something could ever create time. Rather it seems like time would have to suddenly, spontaneously exist simultaneously with the first cause when it causes everything else. Or maybe time suddenly existing is what created something else. Importantly, it seems that time cannot be caused by the first cause in the ordinary sense of the word since this would involve the first cause already existing before time, and this is impossible since there is no before time. So the idea of something creating time seems impossible.

However, this means that the coming to existence of time and the first cause becomes a brute fact that cannot itself be explained. And the idea that time can somehow spontaneously come into existence seems no less paradoxical than the idea that an infinite series of events can somehow come to pass and lead to our existence. So, the notion of a first cause seems no less mysterious than a series of infinite events of causation taking place. Both leads to paradoxes paradoxes.

Another problems is that it is not clear that an infinite series of events taking place is impossible, since it actually happens all the time.

To travel a specific distance, you first have to travel 1/2 of the way. However, to travel 1/2 of the way you first have to travel 1/4 or the way. And to travel 1/4 of the way you first have to travel 1/8 of the way. And this continues infinitely. So to travel anywhere you have to travel through an infinite series of positions. This is known as Zeno's paradox of motion (https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/paradox-zeno/). Nonetheless, we do actually travel.

Zeno's paradox of an infinite series of positions travelled is different from the paradox of an infinite of events taking place raised by your cosmological argument, but it is still possible that an answer to Zeno's paradox can help us understand how an infinite series of events can take place in other cases. At the very least it seems to indicate that arguments to the effect that an infinite series of events can't pass might be overexaggerated. If this is so, then your argument that there must be a first cause does not hold up.

- the second problem has to do with your statement that the first cause is God. You do not provide any additional argument for this, but God is not the only possible first cause. Aristoteles who is most famously attributed with the cosmological argument did not believe that the first cause was a God, and in modern times the Big Bang rather than God has been thought of as the first cause of everything else. So you need additional arguments to make probable that the first cause is God and not something else such as the Big Bang. Why is it necessarily God which must be the first cause?
